links.outcome: Sepsis prediction performance of fine-tuning, retraining, domain adaptation, and fusion strategies across target-data sizes
links.effect: Fine-tuning consistently underperformed (adjusted p < 0.05 vs. DA, fusion, retraining). DA MMD AUROC 0.720, nAUPRC 2.352 vs fusion AUROC 0.712; retraining AUROC 0.719.
links.quote: Key results demonstrate that fine-tuning consistently underperforms across all data sizes (adjusted p < 0.05 vs. DA, fusion, and retraining) even though it has been the go to method in many prior studies that explored this direction.

links.outcome: Distribution shifts between ICU cohorts and their effect on generalization
links.effect: Distribution shifts across HiRID, MIMIC-IV and eICU were quantified; poor generalization under external validation is attributed largely to distribution shift arising from heterogeneity in data.
links.quote: While artificial intelligence (AI) models trained on ICU data show promise for sepsis prediction, their clinical utility is frequently hampered by poor generalization under external validation, largely attributable to distribution shifts arising from heterogeneity in data.
